Subject: MAP: token assumptions, caching & batching — need quick sanity check

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Marco and I dug into the draft MAP and have a couple of urgent asks before we finalize timelines with procurement. The big items are around unit economics (tokens/$) and the operational assumptions behind the cost estimates in the MAP. We want to avoid surprises in the pilot billing.

Quick summary of what we'd like you to confirm:
- Tokens per user estimate: 420 tokens/session average, 1.6 sessions/user/day (this is our internal estimate).
- Caching assumptions: you show prefix caching for 65% of traffic in the MAP; can you confirm whether that is warm KV cache or application-level response caching?
- Batching: MAP lists batching target of 8 requests per batch in steady state. Is that safe for 50p95 latency SLA?
- Fallback model: what's the cost delta if fallback to a smaller quantized model occurs 10% of the time?

We've attached our working spreadsheet (greenline-token-assumptions-v1.xlsx) with traffic curves and a proposed pilot volume. If you can run a quick sanity check and annotate where Redwood's assumptions diverge from ours, we can lock the mutual action dates for pilot kickoff and procurement.

Target: lock MAP and send to legal by 2026-06-18. Are you able to get this analysis back by end-of-day Friday (6/11)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — this is blocking our renewal window.

Thanks,
Gina West
Director of Product
Greenline Health

Attachments: greenline-token-assumptions-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Gina West <gina.west@greenlinehealth.com>, Marco Silva <marco.silva@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: token assumptions, caching & batching — need quick sanity check

Gina / Marco — thanks for the clear note and the sheet. I'm looping Ben on the econ side to validate the per-token math and caching assumptions. I can do an initial pass today and send a short readout.

High-level reactions up-front (I'll annotate the sheet and return):
- Tokens/user/day looks plausible for conversational flows; our sample pilots historically show 300–550 tokens/session depending on prompt priming. 420 is reasonable as a median.
- Prefix caching: in our MAP we assume prefix KV cache (warm in-memory KV across GPUs) for repeated system prompts and long-lived contexts — that typically reduces model compute by ~40–70% on queries that match. That is different from CDN-style response caching which we also support for deterministic outputs. I'll call this out explicitly in the annotated sheet.
- Batching=8: depends on traffic burstiness. At steady-state throughput and with our continuous-batching runtime, batch=8 keeps p95 latency in the low 100s ms on a 2xA100 node for the quantized 8-bit path. If Greenline needs <80ms p95, we need lower batch sizes or more reserved capacity.
- Fallback cost delta: 10% fallback to a quantized variant reduces per-token spend by ~35% but increases CPU/KV overhead slightly. I'll calculate a sensitivity table.

Ben — can you run the tokens/$ sensitivity (prefetch, batching, and fallback scenarios) and add a cost delta table? Target: return annotated sheet + a 1-page MAP note by EOD 6/11.

Thanks,
Dylan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Gina West <gina.west@greenlinehealth.com>, Marco Silva <marco.silva@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: token assumptions, caching & batching — need quick sanity check

Dylan / Gina — ran the sensitivity screens and attached a quick table (see inline). I left the working workbook in the Drive link and attached a snapshot (map-eval-checklist.pdf).

Executive summary (short):
- Baseline tokens/$ (hosted API, standard non-quantized model): $0.00045 per token (model + infra blended at projected pilot utilization). Baseline uses no KV caching and batching=1 for conservative SLA.
- With KV prefix caching (65% hit rate as your sheet): effective billed tokens drop ~45% because cached prefixes eliminate repeated decoder steps; blended cost -> $0.00025 per effective token.
- Batching impact: batching=8 yields ~22–28% cost reduction versus batching=1 at same throughput, but p95 latency increases ~30–60ms depending on warmup and GPU type. Batching benefits scale nonlinearly with request size and model sequence lengths.
- Fallback (10% to quantized variant): blended cost savings of ~12% relative to baseline; if fallback uses a 4-bit quantized model the delta goes up to ~18%.

Attached sensitivity snapshot (also in the Drive):
- Scenario A: conservative (no caching, batching=1) -> pilot monthly cost est: $42,600
- Scenario B: KV caching=65%, batching=4 -> pilot monthly cost est: $25,900
- Scenario C: KV caching=65%, batching=8, 10% fallback to quantized -> pilot monthly cost est: $22,700

Action items for MAP doc: please confirm whether Greenline can commit to the caching integration pattern (we need instrumentation + prefix keying rules) and whether the pilot SLA can accept p95 up to 160ms (current batch=8 estimate) or if you require <100ms. Those choices materially change the reserved capacity and committed spend in the MAP.

Ben Carter
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: map-eval-checklist.pdf (PDF snapshot)

Subject: Re: MAP: token assumptions, caching & batching — need quick sanity check

Thanks everyone — consolidating into the MAP amendment so legal/procurement can move. I captured the key decision points below and added a short acceptance checklist. I'll attach the updated MAP PDF to the Deal record after you confirm.

Decisions required from Greenline (tick and reply):
- [ ] Caching pattern: confirm "KV prefix cache (inference runtime)" vs "CDN/response cache". (Recommended: KV prefix cache for conversational UX)
- [ ] p95 latency tolerance for pilot: choose one: <=100ms || <=160ms (batching tradeoffs documented above)
- [ ] Fallback policy: Accept 10% fallback to quantized variant for burst cost savings? Yes/No
- [ ] Instrumentation handoff: confirm Slack channel + list of engineers for KV keying rules and metrics (we'll need this by pilot kickoff).

MAP amendment notes (summary to be added to Deal):
- If Greenline accepts KV prefix caching AND p95 <=160ms, we will model Scenario C in the MAP (estimated pilot spend ~$22.7k/month) and proceed with the proposed reserved capacity window.
- If Greenline requires <=100ms p95 with no fallback, model Scenario B (~$25.9k/month) and increase reserved capacity to cover lower batching benefits.
- If Greenline declines caching, MAP reverts to conservative baseline (~$42.6k/month) and procurement will require a higher commit.

Next steps / timeline:
- Greenline to confirm checkboxes above by EOD 6/15 so we can finalize MAP and circulate to legal on 6/18.
- Redwood will attach updated MAP + cost appendix to HubSpot and share a short one-pager for procurement.

Kimberly Park
Head of GTM Operations, Redwood Inference
